content.background: Undernutrition is a major problem in Sri Lanka, with 29.4% of children under five being underweight and 13.5% stunted[cite: 1011]. Nearly 30% suffer from iron deficiency anaemia[cite: 1013].
content.critical_period: The first two years are crucial for rapid physical growth and mental development; nutritional insults during this period reduce adult IQ and work capacity[cite: 1014, 1015, 1017].

content.exclusive_duration: Exclusive breastfeeding (EBF) is recommended from birth until the completion of six months (180 days)[cite: 1025].
content.extended_duration: Breastfeeding should continue for two years or more after introducing complementary foods[cite: 1025].
content.early_introduction: Complementary feeding should only be considered after 120 days if growth faltering occurs despite correct breastfeeding or if the mother must be away for long periods[cite: 1033, 1034, 1035].

content.storage_guidelines: Expressed Breast Milk (EBM) can be kept at room temperature for 8 hours, in the refrigerator for 24 hours, and in the freezer for 3 months[cite: 1042].
content.feeding_method: EBM should be fed using a clean cup or cup and teaspoon, avoiding feeding bottles[cite: 1043, 1110].

content.initial_texture: Complementary foods should be introduced in thick, mashed form from the start to provide high energy in small quantities[cite: 1048].

progression.7-8_months: Well-mashed foods; 2-3 meals/day; 1/2 tea cup per meal[cite: 1056].
progression.9-11_months: Coarsely chopped/mashed foods (finger foods); 3-4 meals/day; 3/4 tea cup per meal[cite: 1056].
progression.12-23_months: Family foods (coarsely chopped); 3-4 meals/day; 1 tea cup per meal[cite: 1056].

content.animal_sources: Iron-rich foods like fish, sprats, liver, and meat should be included daily from the 7th month[cite: 1067, 1068].
content.vegetarian_sources: Local iron sources include Gotukola, Sarana, Thampala, Soya, and green gram[cite: 1069].
content.bioavailability_boosters: Add Vitamin C sources (lemon, lime, nelli, guava, banana, papaya) to meals to increase iron absorption from pulses and greens.

content.food_sources: Vitamin A rich foods include liver, egg yolk, yellow pumpkin, yellow sweet potatoes, carrots, papaw, mangoes, and dark green leaves[cite: 1075].
content.egg_introduction: Egg yolk can start at 7 months (well-cooked); egg white starts at 9 months[cite: 1076, 1077].

content.energy_boost: Add 1-2 teaspoons of coconut oil, coconut milk, margarine, or butter to meals to increase energy density and palatability[cite: 1053, 1078].
content.clinical_need: Children with inadequate weight need more fat added to their diet[cite: 1079].

content.milestones: Finger foods start at 8-9 months; self-feeding without assistance should be achieved by 2 years[cite: 1094, 1096].
content.methods: Feed patiently, maintain eye contact, and avoid forced feeding[cite: 1097, 1098, 1100]. Distractions should be minimized during meal times[cite: 1103].

content.lankan_snacks: Yoghurt, curd, boiled gram, green gram, potatoes, or Thriposha[cite: 1082, 1177].
content.traditional_options: After one year, traditional foods like helapa, sago pudding, weli thalapa, and aggala are recommended[cite: 1178].
content.restrictions: Curd should be given without sugar or honey[cite: 1083]. Avoid added sugar or salt during the first year[cite: 1085].

content.fortified_food: Thriposha is provided to infants with growth faltering/underweight from 6 months to one year[cite: 1121].
content.megadose_schedule: Vitamin A (100,000 IU) is given at 9, 18, and 36 months[cite: 1123]. Postpartum mothers receive 200,000 IU within two weeks of delivery[cite: 1127].
content.iron_drops: Preterm and Low Birth Weight (LBW) infants should receive iron supplements from two months of age[cite: 1131, 1132].

content.during_illness: Increase fluid intake and breastfeeding frequency; offer small, energy-dense meals frequently[cite: 1138, 1141, 1144].
content.recovery_period: Give one extra meal daily for at least 2 weeks after illness to prevent growth faltering[cite: 1139].

content.weighing_schedule: Children under 2 years must be weighed monthly; from 2-5 years, weigh once every three months[cite: 1148].
content.length_height: Length measured at 4, 9, and 18 months; height measured every 6 months after age two[cite: 1152].
content.clinic_location: Weighing should occur at clinics until 6 months, and at field weighing posts thereafter[cite: 1150].

content.hand_washing: Caregivers must wash hands with soap before preparation/feeding; children's hands must be washed before eating[cite: 1107].
content.storage: Serve food immediately after preparation; keep cooked food well covered[cite: 1108].
content.avoidance: Do not use feeding bottles; avoid blending or straining food after 8 months[cite: 1087, 1110].

servings.cereals: 1/2 tea cup cooked rice or 1 slice of bread[cite: 1182, 1183].
servings.vegetables: 3 tablespoons cooked fruit vegetables or 1/2 tea cup leafy greens[cite: 1202, 1203].

content.stunting_data: Nutritional problems in Sri Lanka typically appear around the 6th month and rise into the 2nd year, largely due to incorrect complementary feeding[cite: 1018].
content.consequences: Inadequate early nutrition leads to non-communicable diseases, reduced work capacity, and complications during delivery for women[cite: 1017].

content.training_goals: Objectives include training children to munch food to transition to family foods by age one and encouraging self-feeding by age two[cite: 1022, 1023].
content.nutritional_gap: Complementary food is essential because breast milk alone cannot meet increasing nutrient needs after six months[cite: 1021].

content.protection: Exclusive breastfeeding for 180 days reduces the incidence of diarrhoea, respiratory infections, and otitis media[cite: 1029].
content.development: There is evidence that motor and cognitive development is enhanced by exclusive breastfeeding for the full six months[cite: 1030].

content.allergy_signs: Symptoms include excessive crying, urticaria (hives), vomiting, colics, diarrhoea, and wheezing[cite: 1064, 1065].
content.diagnostic_protocol: Introduce only one new food item at a time and continue for 3-4 days to identify potential triggers[cite: 1062].

content.bioavailability_methods: To increase iron absorption in pulses, families should use soaking, germinating, or fermenting techniques[cite: 1071].
content.citrus_addition: Adding a minimal amount of water to citrus fruits like orange or mandarin is acceptable when preparing them for infants[cite: 1074].

content.choking_hazards: Avoid small, rounded, hard pieces of vegetables and whole nuts/pulses[cite: 1086].
content.processing_limits: Avoid blending or straining food after the child reaches 8 months to encourage chewing skills[cite: 1087].

content.cereal_portions: One serving equals 1/2 tea cup of cooked rice, 1 slice of bread, or 3 crackers[cite: 1182, 1183, 1187].
content.tuber_portions: One serving equals 2 egg-sized potatoes or 1 egg-sized sweet potato[cite: 1185, 1186].

content.dairy_portions: One serving equals 100ml of liquid milk, 1 cup of yoghurt/curd, or 3 heaped teaspoons of milk powder[cite: 1190, 1191, 1193].
content.cheese_portion: One serving of cheese is a piece roughly the size of a small matchbox[cite: 1192].

content.protein_portions: One serving equals 3 tablespoons of cooked dhal, 6 sprats, or 25-50g of cooked meat[cite: 1196, 1199].
content.egg_conversion: One serving of eggs equals 1 hen's egg or 1.5 duck's eggs[cite: 1197, 1198].

content.postpartum_care: All postpartum mothers should receive Vitamin A mega dose 200,000 IU within two weeks of delivery[cite: 1127].
content.infant_vitamin_a: The 100,000 IU mega dose is given at 9 months (with measles vaccine) and 18 months[cite: 1123].

content.stunting_protocol: If a child is stunted or at risk, length should be measured every two months up to age two, and height every three months thereafter[cite: 1153].
content.standard_height_checks: For healthy children, length/height is measured at 4, 9, and 18 months, and every 6 months after age two[cite: 1152].

content.serving_unit: 1/2 a tea cup of cooked rice or 1 slice of bread[cite: 1182, 1183].
content.bread_standard: A 450g loaf of bread should be sliced into 9 equal pieces[cite: 1183].

content.meat_visual: A piece the size of a matchbox equals roughly 25-50g[cite: 1199].

content.sugar_timing: Sugar-based foods should only be given in small amounts after mealtime[cite: 1091].

content.snack_definition: A small quantity of energy-dense food or drink taken between main meals (breakfast, lunch, dinner)[cite: 1175].
content.snack_purpose: To provide a brief supply of energy and temporarily tide hunger[cite: 1176].

content.yam_snacks: Boiled potatoes, sweet potatoes, or any other yam served with scraped coconut[cite: 1177].
content.fried_snacks: Fried potatoes, sweet potatoes, or ash plantains[cite: 1177].

content.traditional_lankan_snacks: Helapa, sago pudding, weli thalapa, and aggala are recommended after the first year[cite: 1178].

content.bun_measurement: One serving equals 1/2 of a tea bun[cite: 1184].
content.cereal_measurement: One serving equals 3 tablespoons of breakfast cereals[cite: 1188].

content.maternal_supplements: All breastfeeding mothers should receive Iron, folic acid, Vitamin C, and Calcium for at least six months[cite: 1126].
content.maternal_food_support: Thriposha should be provided to breastfeeding mothers for a minimum of six months[cite: 1126].

content.standard_iron_dosage: 2mg per kg of body weight per day[cite: 1129].
content.community_programme_dose: 12.5mg of elemental iron daily for 2 months, or every other day for 4 months[cite: 1130].

content.preterm_iron_start: Low birth weight (LBW) and preterm infants should begin iron supplements from two months of age[cite: 1131].
content.preterm_iron_duration: Supplementation should continue until at least one year, and preferably up to two years[cite: 1132].

content.vitamin_a_9_months: 100,000 IU given with the measles vaccine[cite: 1123].
content.vitamin_a_18_months: 100,000 IU given with the 4th dose of OPV/DPT/Hep.B[cite: 1123].
content.vitamin_a_3_years: 100,000 IU given with the Measles and Rubella vaccine[cite: 1123].

content.fluid_intake: Fluid intake and the frequency of breastfeeding must be increased during illness[cite: 1141].
content.appetite_loss: If appetite is poor, offer favorite foods that are soft and appetizing in small, frequent meals[cite: 1142, 1143].

content.illness_meal_size: Offer small meals of 3-5 tablespoons every 2-3 hours[cite: 1144].
content.energy_boost_illness: Add oil, margarine, butter, or ghee to make food more energy-dense during sickness[cite: 1145].

content.standard_weighing: Monthly up to 24 months, then every 3 months until age five[cite: 1148].
content.problematic_growth: Children who are underweight, overweight, or showing growth faltering must be weighed monthly regardless of age[cite: 1149].

content.utensil_hygiene: Clean cups, bowls, and spoons used for feeding children should not be used for any other purposes[cite: 1109].
content.hand_washing_caregiver: Caregivers must wash hands with soap and water before food preparation and feeding[cite: 1107].

content.first_food_consistency: Well-cooked rice mashed to a soft, semi-solid paste is the recommended first complementary food[cite: 1113].
content.progression_timeline: Coarsely mashed foods should be introduced at the end of the 7th month[cite: 1114].

content.finger_food_timing: Introduce finger foods like a small piece of bread or hoppers around 8-9 months[cite: 1115].
content.vigilance: Caregivers must be extremely vigilant to prevent choking when finger foods are introduced[cite: 1115].

content.family_meals: Gradually transition the child to eat together with other family members to encourage learning and eating[cite: 1104].
content.one_year_milestone: A child should be able to eat family foods with less spice by one year of age[cite: 1118].

content.thriposha_eligibility: Infants with growth faltering or who are underweight receive Thriposha from 6 months to one year[cite: 1121].

content.multivitamin_policy: Multivitamin syrups are generally not recommended for infants unless specifically medically indicated[cite: 1125].
content.general_supplements: Any vitamin-mineral supplements for infants must only be given based on medical advice[cite: 1122].

content.weighing_location: Children up to 6 months should be weighed at clinics; after 6 months, they should be weighed at field weighing posts[cite: 1150].
content.incidental_weighing: If a child visits a clinic for any reason, they should be weighed while there[cite: 1151].

content.fruit_portion: One medium banana or one medium orange constitutes one serving of fruit[cite: 1200].

content.cooked_vegetable_portion: 3 tablespoons of cooked fruit-vegetables constitute one serving[cite: 1202].
content.leafy_vegetable_portion: 1/2 of a tea cup of cooked leafy vegetables constitutes one serving[cite: 1203].
